title: GitHub Actions (CI workflows, action pins, Dependabot for actions)

versions.pinnedIn: .github/workflows/ci.yml job validate, step 'Install Claude Code CLI'

versions.version: runners ubuntu-latest (Ubuntu 24.04), windows-latest (Windows Server 2025), macos-latest (macOS 26 arm64)

rules.rule: Keep every `permissions:` block explicit and read-only unless a job needs a write scope; grant a write scope at job level for that job only, never at workflow level. Setting any scope sets every unlisted scope to none.
rules.why: A broad GITHUB_TOKEN turns any compromised step (a malicious dependency's postinstall, an injected command) into a write to the repository; omitting a needed scope makes the job fail with 403 because unlisted scopes become none.
rules.repoConvention: The repo sets `permissions: contents: read` once at workflow level; zizmor's excessive-permissions audit prefers `permissions: {}` at workflow level plus per-job grants. Both jobs only read, so follow the repo; move to per-job grants as soon as one job needs more.

rules.rule: Run code from pull requests only under `pull_request`, never under `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run`; if a privileged trigger is ever needed (labelling, commenting), it must not check out or execute the PR's code, and must not set `allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true` on actions/checkout.
rules.why: pull_request_target and workflow_run run in the base repository's context with its token, secrets and caches; checking out fork code there is a 'pwn request' that can take over the repo. Under `pull_request` a fork gets a read-only token and no secrets. Since checkout v7 the action refuses fork checkout under these triggers unless the opt-in input is set.
rules.since: actions/checkout v7.0.0 (refusal of fork checkout by default)

rules.rule: Never put a `${{ }}` expression carrying event data (anything ending in title, body, message, head_ref, ref, label, name, email, default_branch, page_name) inside a `run:` script. Pass it through `env:` and reference it as a quoted shell variable ("$TITLE"), or pass it as an action input.
rules.why: Expressions are substituted into the script text before the shell runs, so a crafted branch name or PR title breaks out of quoting and executes commands on the runner (recent advisories: command injection via branch names and issue titles).
where: .github/workflows/ci.yml: no run step uses an expression today; expressions appear only in concurrency, name, runs-on and with (not shell contexts)

rules.rule: Pin every action by full 40-character commit SHA with a `# vX.Y.Z` comment, take the SHA from the action's own repository (not a fork), and keep the same SHA for the same action in every job.
rules.why: A tag or branch can be moved to malicious code; a SHA cannot without a SHA-1 collision. A SHA copied from a fork, or two jobs on different SHAs, defeats review of what actually runs.
where: .github/workflows/ci.yml jobs unit and validate (all three actions pinned; SHAs verified against the release tags on 2026-11-09)

rules.rule: Set `persist-credentials: false` on actions/checkout unless a later step runs authenticated git; when a step does need it, set `true` explicitly.
rules.why: By default checkout leaves the token configured for git (since v6 in a file under $RUNNER_TEMP rather than .git/config) for the rest of the job, where any later step, including npm postinstall scripts, can read it.
where: .github/workflows/ci.yml jobs unit and validate (both checkouts use the default true)
rules.repoConvention: The repo uses the default (credentials persisted). The token is read-only (contents: read) and fork PRs get a read-only token, so the exposure is low; recorded as a question rather than a defect.

rules.rule: Keep the Claude Code CLI version pinned exactly in the install step and bump it by hand: Dependabot's github-actions ecosystem does not see npm installs inside `run:`.
rules.why: An unpinned CLI can change what `claude plugin validate --strict` accepts between two runs of the same commit; a forgotten pin silently drifts behind (2.1.307 pinned, 2.1.319 latest).
where: .github/workflows/ci.yml job validate, step 'Install Claude Code CLI'

rules.rule: Give every concurrency group a workflow-specific prefix and cancel in progress only for pull-request runs.
rules.why: Group names are global across workflows and case-insensitive, so a bare `${{ github.ref }}` group lets one workflow cancel another; cancelling on main would leave main without a verdict.
where: .github/workflows/ci.yml concurrency (group ci-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress only for pull_request)

rules.rule: Never use self-hosted runners for this public repository's workflows.
rules.why: Any user can open a PR whose code runs on the runner and persist on or pivot from that machine.
where: not used here yet (all jobs use GitHub-hosted runners)

bugCategories.name: expression-injection-in-run
bugCategories.lookFor: A `${{ github.event.* }}`, `github.head_ref`, `github.ref` or other attacker-controllable context interpolated directly in a `run:` block (or in a script input of an action such as github-script).
bugCategories.failure: Arbitrary command execution on the runner with the job's token and secrets.

bugCategories.name: privileged-trigger-runs-pr-code
bugCategories.lookFor: `pull_request_target`, `workflow_run` or `issue_comment` triggers together with a checkout of the PR head, `allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true`, or use of artifacts produced by a PR run.
bugCategories.failure: Fork code runs with write token and secrets: repository takeover, secret exfiltration, cache poisoning of main.

bugCategories.name: unpinned-or-mismatched-action-ref
bugCategories.lookFor: `uses:` with a tag or branch instead of a 40-char SHA; a SHA whose `# vX` comment does not match the tag it resolves to; the same action at different SHAs in different jobs; a SHA from a fork.
bugCategories.failure: A moved tag silently runs new (possibly malicious) code; reviewers approve a version that is not the one that runs.

bugCategories.name: token-scope-widening
bugCategories.lookFor: `write` scopes or `write-all` at workflow level, a removed `permissions:` block (falls back to repository default), or a new job that writes without a job-level grant.
bugCategories.failure: Excess write access for every step; or a job that fails with 403 because unlisted scopes became none.

bugCategories.name: persisted-credentials-exposed
bugCategories.lookFor: actions/checkout without `persist-credentials: false` followed by third-party code (npm/pip installs with lifecycle scripts) or an upload-artifact of the workspace.
bugCategories.failure: The job token is readable by later steps or leaks in an artifact.

testing.layers: A workflow change is proved only by the CI run it triggers on the pull request: check that every matrix leg ran and the expected jobs appear. Static audit of the YAML (security and syntax) is the cheap layer before that; the repo has none yet.
harness: .github/workflows/ci.yml (the workflow itself is the harness; no workflow linter in the repo)
commands: python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -v (what job unit runs)
claude plugin validate --strict . && claude plugin validate --strict plugins/stackfoundry (what job validate runs)
traps: `-latest` labels move to a new OS version over 1-2 months after an announcement (ubuntu-26.04 is already published); a green run can turn red with no repo change. Pin an OS version on the matrix leg if the Python 3.11 floor must stay reproducible.
Matrix job order is not guaranteed; never make one leg depend on another's side effects.
A fork PR from a first-time contributor may wait for maintainer approval before CI runs: a missing check is not a pass.

wiring.check: Dependabot's github-actions entry uses `directory: /` so it scans .github/workflows; the single `actions` group bumps all actions in one PR so the shared checkout SHA stays identical across jobs.
wiring.failure: A different directory makes Dependabot miss the workflows; ungrouped PRs can leave jobs on different SHAs.

wiring.check: The commands the CI jobs run match the 'Checks before calling a change done' list in .claude/CLAUDE.md.
wiring.failure: Local checks and CI diverge, so a change is called done that CI rejects (or CI stops checking something the docs promise).

security.note: Dependabot creates alerts only for actions referenced by a semantic version, not for SHA-pinned ones. With every action SHA-pinned, vulnerability awareness rests on Dependabot version updates (weekly) and on watching the advisory database; no advisory exists for actions/checkout, setup-python or setup-node as of 2026-11-09.

Workflow dependency lockfiles (.github/workflows/actions.lock, generated by `gh actions-lock`) pin actions and their transitive action dependencies and verify the source repository at run time; GitHub calls this stronger than SHA pinning and Dependabot regenerates entries. Status: public preview per GitHub's changelog of 2026-10-14; InfoQ (2026-11-06) reports GA on 2026-10-28, while the GitHub docs page read still does not state a status. Not adopted here.

Dependabot applies a default 3-day cooldown to version updates (github-actions supports only `default-days`); raising it gives the ecosystem time to detect a compromised release before it reaches a PR here.
`npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.307` runs the package's postinstall script (`node install.cjs`) in a job whose checkout persisted the token; keep the job's token read-only.
